title: Summer river water quality improved at English invertebrate sites in 2018-2025 and did not cause the autumn score stall; the stall came from the two drought years 2022 and 2025
abstract: Question: earlier campaign work found that autumn gains of the river invertebrate score WHPT ASPT stopped in England in 2018-2025, but it had no water-quality (WQ) data after 2017. Did summer WQ become worse, and does it explain the stall? Data: Environment Agency kick samples 2010-2025; the new EA Water Quality API (2.0 million observations at 7,177 river points within 1 km of invertebrate sites); Met Office district summer weather. Design (planned before the WQ models): the contrast d = autumn minus spring ASPT at the same site and year, summer WQ at the nearest point within 500 m, site and year fixed effects, and a next-summer placebo. Results: within points, summer ammoniacal nitrogen fell 10.6% (95% CI 8.9-12.2%) and orthophosphate 18.4% (16.6-20.2%) from 2010-2017 to 2018-2025 in all seven regions; water temperature rose 0.61 C; minimum oxygen did not change. Within years, autumn ASPT was lower with more ammonia (-0.014 per SD) and orthophosphate (-0.019) and higher with more oxygen (+0.018); placebos were near zero. These WQ changes predict a small gain, not the observed loss of d (-0.019, CI -0.037 to -0.001). The 2018-2025 decrease of d came from 2022 and 2025, in all regions; without them the trend was +0.002 per year (CI -0.006 to 0.010). In 2022 the autumn score fell after the drought summer (lowest oxygen, which explains about 6%); in 2025 the spring score was a record high. Linear summer weather terms gave only partial support. WQ monitoring halved in 2017-2018 and stopped in summer 2020. Limits: associations, spot samples, no flow data, 15 usable years, England only.

display.caption: Within-site anomalies of spring and autumn WHPT ASPT and of d = autumn minus spring ASPT (a, b), June-September rain anomaly (c), and within-point anomalies of summer ammonia, orthophosphate, minimum dissolved oxygen and water temperature at matched river WQ points (d-f), 2010-2025. Grey bands mark 2022 and 2025. Bars are 95% CI.

Within-year slopes of d (a) and autumn ASPT (b) on summer WQ per one within-point SD, with site + year (blue) and site + region-year (green) fixed effects; orange is the placebo with the next summer's WQ. Bars are 95% CI clustered by site.
(a) Mean within-site anomaly of d by EA region and year, 5,373 sites; 2022 and 2025 are low in all seven regions. (b) Spring and autumn parts of d: 2022 is an autumn loss, 2025 a spring gain.

citations.reason: Reported the open 2018-2025 autumn ASPT stall; we test water quality and weather as causes with post-2017 WQ data and find that two years make the stall.
Showed that storm-overflow spills did not explain the stall; source of the panel and fixed-effects code that we reuse.
